title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
authors: Chengsong Huang, Zifeng Wang, Rujun Han, Jun Yan, Yanfei Chen, Zoey CuiZhu, Ke Jiang, Peng Xia, Han Yu, Yufan Zhuang, Yifei Ming, Jiaqi Pan, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Jiaxin Huang, Burak Gokturk, Tomas Pfister, Chen-Yu Lee
lab: Google Cloud AI Research, with Google Cloud, Washington University in St. Louis and UNC Chapel Hill (Chengsong Huang is at Washington University in St. Louis; the work was done during his internship at Google Cloud AI Research)
date: 20 August 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far)

code.title: google-research/envharness, Apache-2.0
code.note: Released with the paper (repository created 7 August 2026, last push 21 August 2026): the ActionableEnv interface, the three components (named Setup, Rules and Link in the code), six Bridges (Toy24, ALFWorld, SWE-bench, OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench, WebArena; the paper counts seven with WebShop, which appears only as an adaptation inside the optional verl-agent patch), the designer agent, per-benchmark corpus configs with their designer prompts, reproduce scripts, and the GRPO integration with verl-agent for ALFWorld. The configs default to gpt-4.1-mini; the paper's tables used Gemini. The README and the entry path take about 20 minutes

takeaway: An agent harness for environments: wrap frozen training environments with composable Stage/Contract/Chain components at the reset/step interface (keeping the trusted human-built verifier) while EnvRigger auto-customizes them against the target policy's diagnosed weaknesses, beating static and generated environments for skill learning and GRPO RL and still scaling where they flatten.
verdict: Believe the design: wrapping a frozen environment at its reset/step interface keeps the original verifier, ports across five very different benchmarks, and the released code does what the paper says. Treat the sizes of the gains as provisional: most single margins sit within three-run noise, the RL comparison is one run per arm, and the paper's own Figure 5 shows the original environments gaining as many tasks as EnvHarness after the first 100 environments.

resources.t: EnvHarness project page, with a live playground
resources.n: the paper's idea in short sections, plus an in-browser Python playground on the 24 game where you edit a Stage, Contract or Chain and apply it to a live Toy24Env: the release's own reference environment, complementary to the household toy on this page.

the practical entry point: provider setup, the per-benchmark reproduce scripts, how to add a Bridge or a new harness layer, and the results tables. The corpus.yaml files hold each benchmark's designer prompt and acceptance rule.

resources.t: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
resources.n: the skill extraction and retrieval pipeline every skill-learning result here runs through; EnvHarness changes only where the trajectories come from.

resources.t: GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators
resources.n: the ALFWorld baseline: an LLM simulates the environment at the edge of the agent's ability. EnvHarness's main argument against it is that simulated transitions and verdicts can drift.

resources.t: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites (VeriEnv)
resources.n: the WebArena baseline: clones websites into executable synthetic environments with programmatic rewards.

resources.t: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
resources.n: the SWE-bench baseline: synthesizes new repository task instances by breaking working code. Figure 5 compares it with EnvHarness at equal environment counts.

resources.t: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design (PAIRED)
resources.n: the classic statement of the problem EnvHarness inherits: environments should be designed against the current policy, at the edge of what it can do.

resources.by: Jiang, Grefenstette and Rocktäschel, arXiv 2010.03934, ICML 2021
resources.n: the curriculum view: replay the levels with the most learning signal. EnvRigger's band of target success rates is a hand-written version of the same idea.

resources.t: Don't Just Fine-tune the Agent, Tune the Environment
resources.n: the closest earlier work on reshaping what the environment says back to the learner (corrective feedback, reward shaping), which the paper cites as hand-designed.
the agent-harness side of the paper's central analogy, one of the three harness write-ups it cites.
the RL framework the release patches, at a pinned commit, to run GRPO inside EnvHarness environments: ALFWorld by default, with WebShop only in the optional full patch.

kb.t: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
kb.n: the authoring route EnvHarness argues against: build 37,300 new terminal environments from recorded agent runs. EnvHarness instead wraps the environments that already exist and keeps their verifiers; the two could combine (wrap the generated worlds).

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: the agent-harness side of the analogy, measured: models building and evolving the wrapper around a frozen model. Its warning that evolution gains are unstable and executor-specific applies to EnvRigger's write-and-validate loop as well.

kb.t: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
kb.n: another way to close the loop between a harness and training data: the serving router orders a curriculum. EnvHarness closes it on the environment side, with diagnosed weaknesses choosing the next environment.

kb.t: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
kb.n: where GRPO comes from, the algorithm of the RL experiment (Table 4).

kb.t: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
kb.n: the RL with verifiable rewards lineage; EnvHarness keeps rewards verifiable by never touching the original verifier.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: the skill abstraction EnvHarness feeds through ReasoningBank-style extraction; its finding that skills act as procedural anchors fits the skills shown in Appendix F, which are procedures forced by the components.

kb.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
kb.n: the think-then-act interaction loop the policies here run (the ALFWorld policy is prompted to reason in think tags, then act); ReAct also introduced ALFWorld as an LLM-agent benchmark.

topics.n: RL for LLM agents and curricula: GRPO in reshaped environments, and policy-conditioned environment design (PAIRED, Prioritized Level Replay, POET).
agent post-training and RL with verifiable rewards, where environment supply is becoming the bottleneck.
the agent harness the paper's analogy starts from: tools, memory and skills around a frozen model.
ALFWorld, WebArena, SWE-bench Verified, OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench and WebShop, the benchmarks wrapped here.
